planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; hybridized by Heidi Douglas, it won the AHS Extra Large Diameter Award in 2025.

directions: Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, spacing clumps to allow air circulation around the oversized blooms. Hybridized by Heidi Douglas, Boss Hogg carries flowers registered at seven inches or more in diameter, the minimum bloom size required for the American Hemerocallis Society's Extra Large Diameter Award, and it won that national honor in 2025. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the large flowers coming on strong scapes.

directions: Grow in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, giving plants ample room since award-class extra-large blooms perform best with good light and air movement. Registered by hybridizer Murphy, Poly Nation bears flowers of at least seven inches across, meeting the American Hemerocallis Society's size threshold for its Extra Large Diameter Award, which the cultivar won in 2024. Divide crowded clumps every few years in spring to sustain vigorous bloom.
